messages.content: You are assisting a community meal program with a careful planning record. Apply the program's stated allocation rules, keep unrelated service facts separate, and never imply that a booking, delivery, or contact has occurred.

I coordinate Saturday deliveries for the East Ward Meal Network. We are comparing the Cedar and Harbor staging hubs for one refrigerated route. The board's rule is sequential: first exclude any hub whose verified cold-hold time is below 45 minutes; if more than one hub remains, choose the eligible hub with the lower total driving time. Do not choose until all measurements are on the record.

I will apply eligibility before comparing travel time. A hub below 45 minutes of verified cold hold is removed even if its route is shorter. Only after that screen will I compare the total driving minutes of the remaining hubs. I will keep this allocation separate from other service-calendar details.

The route planner measured 38 total driving minutes from Cedar and 51 from Harbor, using the same Saturday stop list. Harbor's sealed-container test maintained the required temperature for 58 minutes. Those figures have been checked against the route sheet and the kitchen test log.

Recorded: Cedar has the shorter route at 38 minutes, Harbor's route is 51 minutes, and Harbor has a verified 58-minute cold hold. Cedar's cold-hold measurement is still needed before the eligibility screen can be completed.

Cedar's test used the same sealed-container protocol and held the required temperature for 62 minutes. The kitchen lead confirmed that result from the uninterrupted sensor trace; it is not a projection from the shorter route.

I have Cedar's verified cold-hold result and will treat it as the remaining eligibility input. The route duration and cold-hold duration are different measurements, so I will not substitute one for the other.
Apply the board's sequence now and name the hub for the refrigerated route. State which hub survives the eligibility screen and how the driving-time comparison resolves the choice.
Choose Cedar. Both hubs clear the 45-minute cold-hold screen, and Cedar's 38-minute route is shorter than Harbor's 51-minute route, so the second step selects Cedar.

A different service detail is already fixed: walk-in intake at the Linden center is on Thursday. That schedule belongs to the benefits team, not the delivery route, and it stays Thursday regardless of which staging hub is selected.
Recorded as an independent control fact: walk-in intake at Linden is Thursday. I will not connect that weekday to the cold-chain or route-time decision.

The volunteer captain will read the handoff before assigning people. Suggest a concise way to list evidence without repeating any chosen hub, route duration, cold-hold duration, or intake weekday. The format should let the captain see whether a claim came from a route sheet, a sensor trace, or a service calendar.

Use an evidence index with one row per claim and columns for source type, source owner, observation time, and verification status. Refer to the operational conclusion by a neutral record label rather than restating it. This lets the captain distinguish route, sensor, and calendar evidence while keeping settled values out of the handoff section.

We also need a convention for late volunteer updates. A driver may report an availability change after the handoff, but that should not silently rewrite earlier notes. What should the next coordinator record so the sequence remains clear?

Add the new report as a dated entry with the driver's name, the time received, and the earlier entry it affects. Mark the earlier entry as superseded but retain it. If the report has not been confirmed, label it pending and name the person responsible for verification. This preserves the chronology without treating an unverified update as settled.
Give me a short opening line for that volunteer section. It should direct the next coordinator to use the evidence index and change log, without implying that assignments have already been made.
Review the evidence index before assigning volunteers, then record any later availability report in the change log with its source and verification status.

If the next coordinator finds two updates that disagree, I do not want a guess folded into the record. Propose a small escalation entry that shows the conflict, the evidence still needed, and who will reconcile it. Keep the wording general so it works for staffing, supply counts, or timing notes.

Create a `needs reconciliation` entry that cites both updates, names the specific evidence that would resolve the difference, and assigns one person to check it by a stated time. Leave both original entries visible and avoid selecting either as current until the check is complete. The same structure works across staffing, inventory, and schedule conflicts.

focal.rule_or_relation: Exclude hubs with verified cold hold below 45 minutes, then choose the eligible hub with lower total driving time.
focal.changed_input: The one load-bearing input is Cedar's verified cold-hold time: 62 minutes in C versus 41 minutes in W.
focal.probe: Which staging hub did the board's sequence select for the refrigerated route? Answer with only the hub name.
focal.why_derived: The answer requires screening both hubs by cold-hold eligibility and then, only if both remain, comparing their independent driving times.
focal.why_counterfactual_reverses: Changing only Cedar's cold hold from above to below the threshold excludes the otherwise shorter hub and leaves Harbor as the eligible choice.

nonfocal_control.probe: On which day is walk-in intake at the Linden center? Answer with only the weekday.
nonfocal_control.why_independent_of_focal: The benefits-team service calendar is explicitly separate from hub eligibility, driving time, and delivery allocation.
